'Row build with a deleted work order, per row, or a row you can't start
'Yes
'With the run-on work order deleted the row can no longer be built from at all, and the fill-only user's dash no longer carries a permission explanation.

'Deleted run-on work order: before (22 Sep spec), 'only the new-work-order target is offered', so the row showed a build button with 'A new work order'. Now (14 Oct spec): 'the row offers no build action and its action cell shows a dash'. Fill-only user on a closed work order: before, 'The row will show a dash with an explanation that creating a work order requires "Work Orders — Create & Edit". The explanation must be readable on a phone'; now 'has no available action. The row shows a dash.'

'S6-E1: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
S6-E3: between 29 Sep 2026 and 13 Oct 2026 (not in the change log)
S5-E3: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)

'If the run-on work order has been deleted, only the new-work-order target is offered.
A user who can fill inspections but cannot create work orders, on a row whose work order is closed, sees a dash with an explanation that creating a work order requires 'Work orders - Create & Edit', readable on a phone.

'With the run-on work order deleted, the row offers no build action at all; its action cell shows a dash.
For a user who can fill inspections but cannot create work orders, a row whose work order is closed shows just a dash, with no explanation about permissions.

'1. With the run-on work order deleted, confirm only the new-work-order target is offered.
3. As the fill-only user on a closed-work-order row, confirm the row shows a dash with an explanation that creating a work order requires 'Work orders - Create & Edit', readable on a phone with no hover.

'1. Delete the run-on work order of a Needs action row.
2. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
3. Check that row offers no build action and its action cell shows a dash.
4. Sign in as the fill-only user and open the asset's Inspections tab.
5. Find the row whose work order is closed.
6. Check its action cell shows only a dash, with no build action and no explanation text.

'The change for the fill-only user has no change-log entry; it happened somewhere between 22 Sep and 13 Oct. That the explanation must not appear is inferred from the spec's general rule that no explanatory text is added unless a requirement asks for it; the new spec simply drops the explanation. The spec also says a row built from before the deletion shows its outcome; that cannot happen to a row that needs action, so it is left out.

'The work order note and Audit Log match, including the line count
'Yes
'The asset row no longer shows the number of lines ('3 lines added'); it reads 'Lines added' or 'WO created'.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'Both records will state how many lines were created, and the asset row will read "3 lines added" rather than "Lines added"'. Now (14 Oct spec): 'Both records will state how many lines were created' - the asset-row clause is deleted, and the asset row uses the same outcome words as everywhere else ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …'). The tester now sees 'Lines added …' with no count instead of '3 lines added'.

'S7-R8: between 29 Sep 2026 and 13 Oct 2026 (not in the change log)
S5-R9: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
'Both records state how many lines were created, and the asset row reads for example "3 lines added" rather than "Lines added".

'The asset's Inspections tab row shows the outcome without a count: 'Lines added' when the lines went onto the existing work order, or 'WO created' when a new one was created, linking to that work order.
'3. Confirm both state how many lines were created, and the asset row reads e.g. '3 lines added' rather than 'Lines added'.

'1. Open the asset's Inspections tab and find the inspection's row.
2. Check the row reads 'Lines added' (or 'WO created') with no line count, and links to the work order.

'No change-log entry. The 22 Sep spec was inconsistent (another line already said 'Lines added'), and the 22 Sep design showed 'Lines added' with the work order number; the new spec matches the design. 'Lines are kept if the note or Audit Log fails, deleted records handled
'Yes
'When the line carrying the inspection is split onto a new work order, the inspection's report note now moves with it, while the build note and Audit Log entry stay on the original.

'Before (22 Sep spec): after a split, 'the note and the Audit Log entry stay on the original. The new work order carries no inspection provenance', so the inspection report note stayed on the original. Now (14 Oct spec) adds: 'The inspection's report notes are not records of the build: when a line with an inspection is split onto a new work order, those notes move with the line and are removed from the original.' After splitting the line that carries the inspection, the report note is on the new work order and gone from the original.

'S7-E4: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
SV-10913: 6 Oct 2026 (Milos Vasic in Jira)
'If the work order is later split, the note and the Audit Log entry stay on the original, and the new work order carries no inspection provenance.

'After a split, the 'built from inspection' note and the Audit Log entry stay on the original work order; the new work order gets neither (unchanged).
When the line that carries the inspection is split onto the new work order, the inspection's report note moves with it: it appears on the new work order's Notes tab and is removed from the original.
'4. Split the work order; confirm the note and Audit Log entry stay on the original and the new work order carries no inspection provenance.

'1. On the work order with the build, select the line that carries the inspection.
2. Split it onto a new work order.
3. Open the original work order's Notes tab and Audit Log.
4. Check the 'built from inspection' note and the Audit Log entry are still there.
5. Check the inspection report note is no longer on the original work order.
6. Open the new work order's Notes tab and Audit Log.
7. Check the inspection report note is there, and there is no 'built from inspection' note or Audit Log entry.

'Decided by the product manager on 6 Oct and written into the spec the same day. Use a fresh split: work orders split before this rule keep their notes where they are. The first expected line is unchanged and kept so the tester can tell the two notes apart.

'ShopCoach with no results, failures, leaving the page and several axles
'Yes
'Two flagged tires on the same row now reach ShopCoach as one finding instead of one per tire, and a draft that fails a second time no longer leaves one empty line per finding.

'Row as one finding: before (22 Sep spec), 'each flagged position reaches ShopCoach with its own axle and row', so two flagged tires on Axle 1 Tire pressure were two findings (two skeleton rows while drafting). Now (14 Oct spec): 'each flagged row reaches ShopCoach as its own finding, with its axle, its row and its flagged positions' - one finding, one skeleton row. Failure: before, 'When the assistant call fails the user is offered a retry, and after a second failure one empty line per finding'. Now: the user 'can try again ... No empty lines are created.' The difference shows only after a second failure: before, one empty line per finding; now none.

'S15-E2: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S15-E5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)

'If the call to ShopCoach fails, the user is told that it failed, and is never left with an empty panel.
If the same field is flagged on several axles, each flagged position reaches ShopCoach with its own axle and row so they are not collapsed into one line.

'Each flagged measurement row is one finding: two flagged tires on the same row and axle go to ShopCoach as one finding naming the axle, the row and both flagged positions. While drafting there is one skeleton row for that finding, and the proposed line names that row's finding.
If drafting fails, you are told it failed and can try again with Try Again (unchanged).
If it fails again, no empty lines are created and nothing is added to the work order.

'1. Note for the tester: forcing ShopCoach to return nothing or to fail cannot be done by hand — it is a developer/automated check. By hand, if an empty or failed result occurs naturally, confirm the user is told plainly and the work order is unchanged (never a blank panel).
4. Check a field flagged on several axles produces a separate proposed line per flagged position (its own axle and row), not one merged line, and that a Monitor finding appears as a watch item rather than work to do now.

'1. Fill the per-axle field so Axle 1 Tire pressure has two flagged tires (for example left outer and right outer Not OK) and Axle 2 Tire pressure has one.
2. Complete the inspection, press Build lines and choose a target.
3. While drafting, count the skeleton rows: one for each flagged field and one for each flagged row, so Axle 1 Tire pressure, with two flagged tires, adds one row, not two.
4. When the proposed lines arrive, check they name one Axle 1 · Tire pressure finding that lists both flagged tires.
5. If drafting fails, read the message shown and check it says the drafting failed and offers Try Again.
6. Press Try Again; if it fails again, check no empty lines appear and nothing is added to the work order.

'Decided on 29 Sep. Drafting failure cannot be forced by hand, and the difference shows only on a second failure, so that part is a developer or automated check; a tester can check it by hand only if the failure happens on its own (for example when ShopCoach cannot be reached). Being told it failed and offered Try Again was already true on 22 Sep. The spec requires at least one line per finding and does not stop ShopCoach proposing more than one line for a finding, so 'not one line per tire' is not expected. A developer has said one line may cover several findings and that the system adds a plain line for any finding left uncovered; that has no product manager sign-off and sits uneasily with 'no empty lines are created', so it is an open product question and is not part of the expected result. Flagged rows on different axles staying separate is unchanged and is left out.
